name: Downtown Nassau
tagline: Bay Street, the straw market and the cruise berths
description: The historic centre along Bay Street, with the pastel colonial government buildings, the Pompey Museum in a former slave market, and a retail strip built almost entirely around cruise passengers. It empties completely when the ships leave.
bestFor: Short stays wanting the historic core and the ferry docks
pros: Colonial architecture and the Pompey Museum
Ferries to Paradise Island and the Family Islands
Jitneys to the whole island from here
cons: Deserted and best avoided after dark

name: Cable Beach
tagline: The resort strip west of the city
description: The main hotel corridor a few kilometres west of downtown, built along a long stretch of sand with Baha Mar's resorts and casino at its centre. It is the most developed and most expensive part of New Providence.
bestFor: Anyone who wants a resort strip with restaurants and a good beach
pros: Jitneys along West Bay Street constantly

name: Paradise Island
tagline: Across the bridge, and priced accordingly
description: The island across the harbour from downtown, reached by two bridges, dominated by the Atlantis resort complex and its water park, with Cabbage Beach along the northern shore. It is self-contained and almost entirely a resort economy.
bestFor: Anyone who wants Atlantis and Cabbage Beach at the door
pros: Cabbage Beach is the best on the island
cons: Among the most expensive addresses in the Bahamas

name: Sandyport and West Bay Street
description: A gated canal-front development and the residential stretch of West Bay Street around it, with supermarkets, a marina village of shops and restaurants, and a largely expatriate and professional Bahamian population. It is the practical residential choice for long stays.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting security, supermarkets and a beach nearby
pros: Safer than most of New Providence

name: Eastern Road
tagline: The old money side, quiet and green
description: The residential road running east along the northern shore, with larger houses, mature gardens and the Bahamas National Trust's Retreat Garden. It is quieter and greener than anywhere else on New Providence and further from the tourist economy.
bestFor: Anyone wanting space and quiet with a car
pros: The greenest and quietest part of the island
The Retreat Garden and Montagu Beach
Away from the cruise economy entirely
cons: Housing is mostly large houses rather than flats
